metadata.title: World Problems Backbone — Unified Data Spine
metadata.description: Unified data backbone for modeling and solving global problems (hunger, conflict, climate, economy). Each country is a row; all dimensions join by iso3.

enrichments.source: Global public data enrichment (WHO, World Prison Brief, IEA, OECD, FAO)
enrichments.scope: 200-country enrichment: health workers, prison rates, renewable energy %, tax burden %, PISA scores, food insecurity, electricity access

enrichments.source: SDG parallel equations (6 domains): gap computation from backbone + cost estimates from World Bank, WHO, IEA, UNESCO, IPCC, Oxfam/G20
enrichments.scope: sdg_equations section: SDG 6 (water), 3 (health), 7 (energy), 4 (education), 13 (climate), 10 (inequality) — computed gaps, published cost-to-fix, affordability framing

enrichments.source: WHO Global Health Observatory (GHO) — mental health indicators
enrichments.scope: mental_health dimension: suicide rates, MH workforce (psychiatrists, psychologists, nurses), MH beds, government MH expenditure, alcohol consumption & disorders — all ~200 countries
enrichments.description: Mental health data from WHO GHO API (MH_*, SA_* indicator series). Age-standardized suicide rates cover 190 countries; workforce/infrastructure indicators have partial coverage (78-146 countries).

meta.framework: UN Sustainable Development Goals — parallel equations to SDG 2 (Zero Hunger)
meta.methodology: Each equation derives the gap from real per-country data in this backbone, then applies a published cost-to-fix estimate from authoritative sources. The 'affordability' framing parallels the hunger equation: how many days of world military spending would close each gap.
sources_overview: World Bank (water/sanitation spending gap, UHC financing)
Oxfam / G20 Brazilian Presidency (global wealth tax proposals)
meta.quick_wins_label: $422B/yr buys safe water + healthcare + electricity + education for everyone

sdg6_water.title: Water & Sanitation
sdg6_water.subtitle: Safe water for everyone
sdg6_water.moral_framing: 2 billion people lack safe water. The equation writes itself.

cost.source: World Bank (SDG 6 WASH spending shortfall: $131.4–140.8B/yr; $114B midpoint cited by WHO/UN-Water)
cost.description: Annual investment shortfall to achieve universal safe water and sanitation by 2030

affordability.framing: Less than 5% of world military spending buys safe water for every human alive.

interventions.name: Rural piped water systems
interventions.roi_note: Prevents 1.4M child deaths/year from diarrheal disease

interventions.name: Safely managed sanitation
interventions.roi_note: Every $1 invested returns $4.30 in avoided healthcare costs (WHO)

interventions.name: Water treatment & quality monitoring
interventions.roi_note: Reduces waterborne disease outbreaks by 60%

interventions.name: Hygiene education & facilities
interventions.roi_note: Handwashing alone prevents 1M deaths/year

sdg6_water.sdg_target: Universal access to safe water and sanitation by 2030

sdg3_health.title: Healthcare Access
sdg3_health.subtitle: Health for all, not just for those who can pay
sdg3_health.moral_framing: 0.1 doctors per 1000 in the Central African Republic. 4.8 in Norway. The gap is the argument.

current_gap.label: 186 of 194 countries below WHO staffing threshold (4.45/1000)

cost.source: World Bank (UHC financing gap in 54 poorest countries by 2030)
cost.description: Additional annual health spending needed in the world's poorest countries to achieve universal health coverage

affordability.framing: For the cost of 27 days of global military spending, every person in the poorest countries could have healthcare.

interventions.name: Train & deploy health workers
interventions.roi_note: Closes the WHO-projected 10M worker shortage by 2030

interventions.name: Primary care clinics & essential medicines
interventions.roi_note: Prevents 5M preventable deaths/year

interventions.name: Maternal & child health programs
interventions.roi_note: Reduces child mortality by 50% in target countries

interventions.name: Disease prevention & vaccination
interventions.roi_note: Eradicates preventable diseases (measles, polio, malaria)

sdg7_energy.title: Energy Access
sdg7_energy.subtitle: Electricity is not a luxury — it is a prerequisite for everything else
sdg7_energy.moral_framing: 524 million people live in darkness. Not because the technology is hard. Because the money goes elsewhere.

cost.source: IEA (Africa alone needs $15B/yr; global electrification ~$35B/yr through 2030)
cost.description: Annual investment to connect the 524M without electricity, primarily via mini-grids and solar

affordability.framing: 5 days of world military spending would electrify the planet.

interventions.name: Mini-grid & off-grid solar
interventions.roi_note: Lowest-cost solution for 60% of unconnected populations (IEA)

interventions.name: Grid extension & last-mile connections
interventions.roi_note: Connects peri-urban and near-grid rural communities

interventions.name: Clean cooking solutions
interventions.roi_note: 4M die yearly from household air pollution — more than malaria + tuberculosis combined

sdg7_energy.sdg_target: Universal access to affordable, reliable energy by 2030

sdg4_education.title: Education
sdg4_education.subtitle: Literacy is the first act of liberation
sdg4_education.moral_framing: 3% literacy in some countries. 99% elsewhere. The same species. The same century.

cost.source: UNESCO (SDG 4 funding gap in low/lower-middle-income countries by 2030)
cost.description: Annual shortfall in education spending to achieve universal quality education

affordability.framing: 15 days of military spending covers a year of quality education for every child.

interventions.name: Universal primary & secondary schooling
interventions.roi_note: 260M children out of school globally (UNESCO)

interventions.name: Teacher training & recruitment
interventions.roi_note: 44M more teachers needed by 2030 to meet SDG 4

interventions.name: Adult literacy programs
interventions.roi_note: Targets the 773M illiterate adults worldwide

interventions.name: Digital learning infrastructure
interventions.roi_note: Bridges the digital divide in education access

sdg4_education.sdg_target: Inclusive, equitable quality education for all by 2030

sdg13_climate.title: Climate Action
sdg13_climate.subtitle: The largest equation in human history — and the only one with a deadline
sdg13_climate.moral_framing: Qatar emits 41 tons of CO2 per person. The DRC emits 0.05. A 764x gap. The countries least responsible will suffer first.

current_gap.label: 37.4 Gt CO2/year — must reach net zero by 2050

cost.source: McKinsey / IPCC AR6 (net-zero transition: $3.5–9.2T/yr globally; $4.3T midpoint for energy system transformation)
cost.description: Total annual capital spending needed across energy, transport, buildings, and industry to reach net-zero by 2050

affordability.framing: The climate transition costs 1.8 years of total military spending. Inaction costs 10–100x more.

interventions.name: Renewable energy infrastructure
interventions.roi_note: Solar/wind now cheapest electricity in history (IRENA 2024)

interventions.name: Electrification of transport
interventions.roi_note: EV market doubling every 2 years — price parity by 2027

interventions.name: Building retrofits & heat pumps
interventions.roi_note: Buildings = 30% of global emissions; cuts energy bills long-term

interventions.name: Reforestation & nature-based solutions
interventions.roi_note: Could remove 7Bt CO2/year — 20% of current emissions

interventions.name: Grid modernization & storage
interventions.roi_note: Enables 100% renewable systems; battery costs down 89% since 2010

interventions.name: Just transition for fossil-fuel workers
interventions.roi_note: Prevents the political backlash that kills climate policy

sdg13_climate.sdg_target: Limit warming to 1.5°C — reach net-zero CO2 by 2050

sdg10_inequality.title: Inequality
sdg10_inequality.subtitle: The root equation — every other gap is downstream of this one
sdg10_inequality.moral_framing: The richest 1% hold more wealth than the bottom 50%. The money exists. The system redistributes it upward.

current_gap.label: ~1464M in extreme poverty; 15x wealth gap between top and bottom deciles

cost.source: G20 Brazilian Presidency / Oxfam (2% global wealth tax on 3,000 billionaires raises ~$313B/yr)
cost.description: Revenue from a 2% minimum tax on billionaire wealth — enough to end extreme poverty and fund most SDG gaps

affordability.framing: A 2% tax on the world's billionaires alone would fund water, electricity, AND education for everyone. With $50B left over.

interventions.name: Global billionaire wealth tax (2% minimum)
interventions.roi_note: Endorsed by G20 Brazilian Presidency; backed by France, Spain, South Africa

interventions.name: Progressive income tax reform
interventions.roi_note: Closing tax havens recovers $480B/yr in lost revenue (Tax Justice Network)

interventions.name: Universal social protection floors
interventions.roi_note: ILO estimates $200B/yr to extend social protection to the poorest 75 countries

interventions.name: Debt cancellation for low-income countries
interventions.roi_note: 54 countries in debt distress — servicing costs exceed health spending

sdg10_inequality.sdg_target: Reduce inequality within and among countries
